claims.text: As-cast equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase, chemically homogeneous, disordered solid solution.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has moderate hardness and strength.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has high or favorable ductility.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable machinability.
The starting alloy lacks significant chemical short-range order.
The starting alloy lacks significant precipitate phases.
The absence of short-range order and precipitates reduces dislocation pinning and the barriers to dislocation motion.
Reduced dislocation barriers or lattice friction increase plasticity and machinability.
Reduced dislocation barriers or lattice friction limit hardness and strength.
Controlled thermal aging can induce short-range chemical order and/or fine precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi without moving it into a completely different phase regime.
Aging-induced short-range order or fine precipitates act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Aging-induced dislocation obstacles increase lattice friction.
Thermally aged CoCrFeNiTi will have greater hardness than the as-cast alloy.
Thermally aged CoCrFeNiTi will have greater compressive and tensile strength than the as-cast alloy.
Thermally aged CoCrFeNiTi will have lower ductility than the as-cast alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature through 600 °C under quasi-static tensile and compressive loading.

contradictions.description: The conditions say loading should not significantly exceed the elastic limit before plasticity is measured, but the proposed ductility, plasticity, and strength measurements require loading into the plastic regime. The stated loading limit is therefore incompatible or at least operationally unclear.

The falsification rule treats failure of aging to create short-range order or precipitates as falsification of their proposed mechanical effect. Failure to produce the mediator is instead a failed manipulation and cannot by itself falsify the mediator-to-property mechanism.
